findings.issue_text: app/models/blocked_email.rb:16 — `record.save` runs inside User#save's validation transaction, so when the email is actually blocked the save returns false, Rails raises Rollback, and the match_count/last_match_at increment is discarded; the block statistics only survive by accident via the controller's separate `user.valid?` call and are never recorded for any `save`/`save!` path such as User.create_for_email (severity P1, confidence 75, blocking)

app/models/blocked_email.rb:11 — a predicate named `should_block?` performs a DB write from inside a validator, and users_controller.rb:168 (`user.valid?`) plus :172 (`user.save`) invoke it twice per signup, so a `do_nothing` match is counted +2 while a `block` match is counted +1, making match_count meaningless as a metric and making every future `valid?` caller (admin previews, specs, change_username) silently corrupt stats (severity P2, confidence 100, blocking)

app/models/blocked_email.rb:12 — `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` is a byte-exact match on the raw `params[:email]` assigned at user.rb:87 with no downcase/strip, while the domain regex in the same validator (email_validator.rb:20, `Regexp.new(..., true)`) and the rest of the boundary (users_controller.rb:269 `Email.downcase(...).strip`) are case-insensitive/normalized, so `Bad@SpamClub.com` or ` bad@spamclub.com` bypasses the block entirely (severity P1, confidence 100, blocking)

app/models/blocked_email.rb:5 — BlockedEmail never normalizes `email` on write and the migration's unique index (db/migrate/20130724201552_create_blocked_emails.rb:10) is case-sensitive, so an admin-entered `Bad@x.com` is stored verbatim, never matches a signup, and `bad@x.com` can be inserted alongside it as a distinct row; the uniqueness invariant exists only on the un-normalized string (severity P2, confidence 100, blocking)

db/migrate/20130724201552_create_blocked_emails.rb:4 — an exact-address string table is the wrong data structure for a blocklist: `bad+1@spamclub.com`, `b.ad@gmail.com` and any new address at the same provider evade it, and the existing domain-level mechanism (SiteSetting.email_domains_blacklist) already covers the pattern case, so the new model adds a weaker parallel mechanism rather than extending the existing one; rebuttal gate: show an admin workflow where per-address blocking without a pattern/domain field is sufficient (severity P2, confidence 75, advisory)

app/models/blocked_email.rb:1 — the task is "blocked users" but BlockedEmail has no relationship to the existing `users.blocked` flag (user.rb:64 `scope :blocked`), so blocking a user does not block their email and blocking an email does not block the user; two disconnected "blocked" concepts now coexist with no invariant linking them and no user_id/blocked_by/reason on the row; rebuttal gate: point to code that keeps the two in sync (severity P2, confidence 75, advisory)

lib/validators/email_validator.rb:1 — `EmailValidator` registered as `validates :email, email: true` performs no email format validation at all (format is client-side only via Discourse.Utilities.emailValid), so the name asserts an invariant the server never enforces and future callers will rely on `email: true` to reject `"garbage"` when it will not; rebuttal gate: show a server-side format check reachable from User (severity P2, confidence 75, advisory)

app/controllers/users_controller.rb:198 — `errors: user.errors.to_hash` introduces a Hash-shaped `errors` key while the same action's RestClient::Forbidden branch (:214) and check_username (:110, :154) return `errors` as an Array, so one JSON key now has two incompatible shapes in one controller and the JS at create_account_controller.js:189 (`result.errors.join`) and :274 (`result.errors.email`) each assume a different one (severity P3, confidence 100, advisory)

app/controllers/users_controller.rb:199 — `values: user.attributes.slice("name","username","email")` exists only so the client can learn the email it just sent, but createAccount already holds that value in its closure (create_account_controller.js:263 `var email = this.get('accountEmail')`); deleting `values` and pushing the closure's `email` yields identical behavior with less API surface and no echo of user attributes (severity P3, confidence 100, advisory)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js:69 — `rejectedEmails.contains(email)` depends on the server echoing a byte-identical string to the client's `accountEmail`, which only holds because User performs no normalization; the moment the lookup is normalized (as the case-bypass fix requires) the client cache silently stops matching, and in the meantime the specific server reason in `errors.email` is discarded in favor of the generic `user.email.invalid` text (severity P3, confidence 75, advisory)

db/migrate/20130724201552_create_blocked_emails.rb:5 — `action_type` is `null: false` with no DB default while the "default is :block" invariant lives only in `before_validation :set_defaults` (blocked_email.rb:22), so the spec's stated use case of manually loading the table, plus `save(validate: false)`/`update_column`/bulk inserts, must supply the bare enum integer or fail, and nothing at the schema level constrains it to a valid Enum value (severity P3, confidence 75, advisory)

app/models/blocked_email.rb:14 — `record.match_count += 1; record.save` is a read-modify-write on a shared counter with no atomic UPDATE (`increment_counter`/`update_all("match_count = match_count + 1")`), so concurrent signups with the same blocked email lose increments (severity P3, confidence 75, advisory)

app/models/blocked_email.rb:13 — `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` is an exact-case, unstripped match and neither `User.new_from_params` (app/models/user.rb:87 `user.email = params[:email]`, no downcase/strip anywhere in User) nor `BlockedEmail#set_defaults` normalizes, so signing up with `Bad@SpamClub.com` or `bad@spamclub.com ` bypasses a `bad@spamclub.com` block row and an admin-entered mixed-case row never matches anything (severity P1, confidence 100, blocking)

app/controllers/users_controller.rb:168 — `if user.valid? && SiteSetting.call_discourse_hub?` runs full validation before `user.save` at :172 runs it again, so every single signup attempt with a listed address calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?` twice and `match_count` advances by 2 (and `last_match_at` is rewritten) per attempt, corrupting the statistic the spec at spec/models/blocked_email_spec.rb:26 claims to guarantee (severity P2, confidence 100, blocking)

app/controllers/users_controller.rb:269 — `change_email` builds `lower_email`, checks only uniqueness, then `email_tokens.create(email: lower_email)` and enqueues `:authorize_email` with no `EmailValidator`/`BlockedEmail.should_block?` call, so a logged-in user can point their account at a blocked (or domain-blacklisted) address and the site sends mail to it; the block is only discovered, if at all, when `EmailToken.confirm` later saves the user and surfaces as the generic `change_email.error` flash at :293 (severity P2, confidence 75, blocking)

spec/components/validators/email_validator_spec.rb:11 — both specs stub `BlockedEmail.should_block?` and call `validate_each` directly, and no spec in the diff saves a `User` against a real `blocked_emails` row, so the wiring `validates :email, email: true, if: :email_changed?` at app/models/user.rb:47 (the only thing that makes the feature take effect) has zero test coverage and a typo like `emails: true` or a dropped line would pass CI (severity P2, confidence 100, blocking)

lib/validators/email_validator.rb:4 — the `email_domains_whitelist`/`email_domains_blacklist` logic was moved out of `User#email_validator` into a new class but the diff adds no spec for either branch in the new location (the only `context` in email_validator_spec.rb is "blocked email"), so the moved regex/`SiteSetting` gating is unverified after the refactor (severity P2, confidence 75, blocking)

app/controllers/users_controller.rb:198 — the new `errors: user.errors.to_hash, values: user.attributes.slice("name","username","email")` response contract that the JS `rejectedEmails` code depends on has no controller spec in the diff, so a rename of either key silently disables client-side rejection with no test failure (severity P3, confidence 100, blocking)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js:69 — `rejectedEmails` is pushed for ANY `result.errors.email` (uniqueness "has already been taken", domain `not_allowed`, blocked) and the validation then reports the generic `I18n.t('user.email.invalid')` instead of the server's reason, so a user whose address is merely already registered is told the address is invalid and cannot learn why; no JS test covers `rejectedEmails` at all (severity P3, confidence 75, advisory)

db/migrate/20130724201552_create_blocked_emails.rb:10 — `add_index :blocked_emails, :email, unique: true` indexes the raw column while `BlockedEmail.should_block?` does an exact `where(email: email)` and `User#email` is stored un-normalized (`user.email = params[:email]` in app/models/user.rb:87, no downcase on write), so a blocked `Spammer@Foo.com` is bypassed by signing up as `spammer@foo.com` and the unique index permits case-variant duplicate block rows; index should be on `lower(email)` or the model must normalize on write and lookup (severity P2, confidence 75, advisory)

lib/validators/email_validator.rb:13 — `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)` runs unguarded on every User validation with no `table_exists?` fallback, so in the deploy window where this code is live before the migration runs every signup raises PG::UndefinedTable, which app/controllers/users_controller.rb:202 `rescue ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid` swallows and reports as `login.something_already_taken` — a total signup outage disguised as a duplicate-account error (severity P2, confidence 75, advisory)

app/models/blocked_email.rb:14 — `record.match_count += 1 ... record.save` is a read-modify-write on the new `match_count` column with no `increment_counter`/`update_all` or lock, so concurrent signups with the same blocked email lose increments; additionally app/controllers/users_controller.rb:168 `if user.valid? && ...` followed by `user.save` at :172 runs the validator twice per request, so `match_count` advances by 2 per single blocked attempt and the statistic the migration exists to record is systematically wrong (severity P3, confidence 100, advisory)

db/migrate/20130724201552_create_blocked_emails.rb:5 — `t.integer :action_type, null: false` has no DB default and no CHECK constraint; the only default is Ruby-side `before_validation :set_defaults`, so the manual table loads the spec explicitly anticipates (spec/models/blocked_email_spec.rb:13 "If we manually load the table with some emails") fail on NOT NULL unless the loader supplies action_type, and any integer outside the Enum (e.g. 0 if the loader assumes 0-based) is stored and silently treated as not-block by `record.action_type == actions[:block]` (severity P3, confidence 50, advisory)

app/models/blocked_email.rb:8 — `Enum.new(:block, :do_nothing)` references `Enum` with no `require_dependency 'enum'` at the top of the file, while every other file in this repo pulls lib/ classes in explicitly (app/models/user.rb:1 `require_dependency 'email'`, users_controller.rb:1-2), so lib/ is not autoloaded and the first process where BlockedEmail is the first constant to touch Enum (e.g. spec boot loading spec/fabricators/blocked_email_fabricator.rb:3 `action_type BlockedEmail.actions[:block]`, which is evaluated eagerly at Fabricator definition) raises NameError: uninitialized constant BlockedEmail::Enum (severity P1, confidence 50, blocking)

app/models/user.rb:47 — `validates :email, email: true, if: :email_changed?` requires the `EmailValidator` constant to be resolvable at User class-load time, but the diff adds lib/validators/email_validator.rb without adding `lib/validators/` to config.autoload_paths or a `require_dependency 'validators/email_validator'` in user.rb, so loading User raises ArgumentError "Unknown validator: 'EmailValidator'" and takes down every request and spec that touches User (severity P0, confidence 50, blocking)

app/controllers/users_controller.rb:168 — `if user.valid? && SiteSetting.call_discourse_hub?` followed by `user.save` at line 172 runs the User validations twice per signup, and because lib/validators/email_validator.rb:13 calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)` which does `record.match_count += 1; record.save` inside validation, every blocked signup attempt increments match_count by 2 and the spec at spec/models/blocked_email_spec.rb:28 (`.by(1)`) only holds when should_block? is invoked directly, never through the real controller path (severity P2, confidence 100, advisory)

lib/validators/email_validator.rb:4-8 — when `email_domains_whitelist` is set and `value` is nil (presence already failed on a new user), `nil =~ regexp` returns nil so `unless email_in_restriction_setting?` adds a second `user.email.not_allowed` error on top of the presence error, producing "Email can't be blank\nEmail is not allowed from that email provider" in the login.errors message for a merely blank email (severity P3, confidence 75, advisory)

lib/validators/email_validator.rb:13 — Refactor turned the previously pure `email_validator` into a DB-mutating validation (`BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)` does `record.match_count += 1 ... record.save` at app/models/blocked_email.rb:14-16), so when a blocked email is rejected inside `User#save` (users_controller.rb:172) the stats write is rolled back with the failed save transaction and `last_match_at`/`match_count` never record the block that spec/models/blocked_email_spec.rb:12-16 says they exist to record (severity P2, confidence 75, blocking)

app/controllers/users_controller.rb:168 — `create` runs validation twice (`user.valid?` at :168 then `user.save` at :172), which was harmless with the original side-effect-free `User#email_validator` but now invokes `BlockedEmail.should_block?` twice per signup attempt, so match statistics depend on transaction-rollback accidents rather than one-count-per-attempt semantics (severity P3, confidence 50, advisory)

app/models/user.rb:45 — Validator order changed from original (presence/uniqueness of email before `username_validator`, HEAD~2 user.rb:45-47) to `username_validator` first, so `user.errors.full_messages.join("\n")` shown to the user via `login.errors` (users_controller.rb:196) now lists username errors before email errors, a user-visible message change not called for by the task (severity P3, confidence 75, advisory)

app/models/blocked_email.rb:8 — `@actions ||= Enum.new(:block, :do_nothing)` references an `Enum` constant that is defined nowhere in the repo and is not added by this diff, so `set_defaults` (every BlockedEmail create) and `should_block?` (whenever a record matches) raise NameError, turning a blocked signup into a raw 500 instead of a validation error (severity P0, confidence 50, blocking)

app/models/blocked_email.rb:16 — `record.save` runs inside the validation phase of the caller's `User#save`/`save!`, which Rails wraps in a transaction that is rolled back when validation fails, so whenever the block actually fires via a save-only path (e.g. app/models/user.rb:103 `user.save!`) the match_count/last_match_at UPDATE is silently discarded; the controller path only records a hit because of the extra out-of-transaction `user.valid?` at app/controllers/users_controller.rb:168 (severity P2, confidence 75, blocking)

app/controllers/users_controller.rb:168 — `if user.valid? && SiteSetting.call_discourse_hub?` followed by `if user.save` at :172 runs EmailValidator (and its DB write in `BlockedEmail.should_block?`) twice per signup request, so `do_nothing` entries (and any matched entry when the user saves successfully) get match_count incremented by 2 per attempt (severity P3, confidence 75, advisory)

app/models/blocked_email.rb:14 — `record.match_count += 1; record.last_match_at = ...; record.save` is a non-atomic read-modify-write that writes the stale in-memory value back, so concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked email lose increments (should be `increment_counter`/`UPDATE ... match_count = match_count + 1`) (severity P3, confidence 75, advisory)

app/models/blocked_email.rb:16 — the boolean return of `record.save` is ignored and nothing is logged, so a failed save (e.g. a future validation on BlockedEmail) leaves `should_block?` returning true while the statistics update is silently dropped (severity P3, confidence 50, advisory)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js:69 — `if (this.get('rejectedEmails').contains(email))` reports `I18n.t('user.email.invalid')` ("valid email address") for any email the server rejected for any reason (already taken, domain not allowed, blocked), so once the flash is dismissed the persistent inline message misstates the cause and the user cannot tell why the address is refused (severity P3, confidence 75, advisory)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js:17 — `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is a mutable array on the class prototype that is never reset on modal close, so every rejected address stays rejected for the lifetime of the page (and is shared across any instances/tests) with no way to retry after e.g. an admin unblocks the email short of a full reload (severity P3, confidence 50, advisory)

app/models/blocked_email.rb:13 — `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` is an exact-match lookup while `User.new_from_params` (app/models/user.rb:87 `user.email = params[:email]`) never normalizes case, so a blocked `bad@spamclub.com` is bypassed by signing up as `Bad@SpamClub.com`; the task's "comprehensive" validation is under-scoped by omitting email normalization (severity P2, confidence 75, blocking)

app/controllers/users_controller.rb:265 — `change_email` creates an email token and sends mail to `lower_email` without ever consulting `BlockedEmail.should_block?` or the `EmailValidator`, so an existing user can switch to a blocked address through the profile flow; the blocked-email check is scoped only to sign-up (severity P2, confidence 75, blocking)

app/models/blocked_email.rb:1 — no route, admin UI, seed, site setting, or rake task in the change ever creates a `BlockedEmail` row (the spec at spec/models/blocked_email_spec.rb:13 admits "If we manually load the table"), so the shipped validation is inert in production; the task implies a usable blocked-users mechanism, not console-only data (severity P2, confidence 75, blocking)

app/models/blocked_email.rb:8 — `Enum.new(:block, :do_nothing)` introduces a `do_nothing` action that nothing in the change assigns or consumes outside tests; it is speculative generality not traceable to "email validation for blocked users" (severity P3, confidence 75, advisory)

app/models/blocked_email.rb:14 — `record.match_count += 1; record.last_match_at = Time.zone.now; record.save` turns the validation predicate `should_block?` into a statistics writer backed by the untasked `match_count`/`last_match_at` migration columns (db/migrate/20130724201552_create_blocked_emails.rb:6-7); hit-tracking is scope expansion beyond validation and makes every `User#valid?` call mutate the DB (severity P3, confidence 75, advisory)

app/controllers/users_controller.rb:199 — `values: user.attributes.slice("name", "username", "email")` widens the create API contract to echo submitted attributes, yet the only consumer (create_account_controller.js:275 `result.values.email`) already holds the same value in `var email = this.get('accountEmail')` at line 263; the `values` key is untraceable work and `errors: user.errors.to_hash` at line 198 additionally exposes every validation error (password, username) that the client never reads (severity P3, confidence 75, advisory)

lib/validators/email_validator.rb:14 — the new `user.email.blocked` message ("is not allowed.") is distinct from the domain-restriction message ("is not allowed from that email provider...") and the uniqueness message ("has already been taken"), and users_controller.rb:198 now returns it in a structured `errors.email` array, so an unauthenticated POST /users (honeypot values are fetchable from /users/hp.json) lets an attacker enumerate the admin-curated BlockedEmail table one address per request (severity P2, confidence 75, blocking)

app/models/blocked_email.rb:12 — `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` is an exact, case-sensitive match while User.new_from_params (user.rb:87) stores the raw submitted email with no downcase/strip/normalization, so a blocked "bad@spamclub.com" is bypassed by signing up as "Bad@spamclub.com", " bad@spamclub.com", or via plus/dot addressing, and the domain check at email_validator.rb:20 is case-insensitive so the two layers disagree (severity P2, confidence 75, blocking)

app/models/blocked_email.rb:16 — `should_block?` executes an UPDATE (`record.save`, including a uniqueness SELECT) on every unauthenticated signup that hits a listed email, even for action_type :do_nothing, so an attacker can drive unbounded writes and hot-row lock contention on one blocked_emails row and inflate match_count/last_match_at, corrupting the admin statistics the spec says are used to judge the list (severity P3, confidence 50, advisory)

lib/validators/email_validator.rb:20 — the whitelist/blacklist regexp `@(domains)` is unanchored and no server-side email format validation exists in the "comprehensive" validator, so "x@gmail.com.attacker.net" (or "x@gmail.com@attacker.net") satisfies an email_domains_whitelist of "gmail.com" while delivering to an arbitrary domain (severity P3, confidence 75, advisory)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js:17,70-75,274-276 — new `rejectedEmails` short-circuit in `emailValidation` and the `pushObject(result.values.email)` on failed createAccount have zero JS test coverage in the diff; consequence: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is declared on the class prototype (shared across every controller instance) and the `result.values.email` vs `accountEmail` equality the gate relies on is unverified, both of which a controller test simulating one failed submit would expose (severity P1, confidence 100, blocking)

spec/components/validators/email_validator_spec.rb:11,17 — both examples do `BlockedEmail.stubs(:should_block?).with(record.email).returns(...)`, so the validator spec proves only that the validator forwards to a mock; blocked_email_spec tests the model in isolation, and nothing in the diff calls `User#valid?` against a Fabricated BlockedEmail, leaving the wiring `validates :email, email: true, if: :email_changed?` (app/models/user.rb:47), EmailValidator constant resolution from lib/validators, and the headline "blocked email rejects signup" behavior unexercised end to end (severity P1, confidence 75, blocking)

lib/validators/email_validator.rb:4-13 — the whitelist/blacklist branches moved out of `User#email_validator` and the new guard `if record.errors[attribute].blank? and BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)` have no example in email_validator_spec.rb (only the "blocked email" context exists) and spec/models/user_spec.rb is untouched in the diff; dropping the `errors[attribute].blank?` guard or breaking the domain regexp passes every test added here (severity P2, confidence 75, advisory)

app/models/blocked_email.rb:5 — `validates :email, presence: true, uniqueness: true` has no example in spec/models/blocked_email_spec.rb; neither blank-email rejection nor duplicate rejection is asserted, so removing the validation passes the suite (severity P3, confidence 100, advisory)

app/models/blocked_email.rb:16 — `record.save` return value is discarded inside `should_block?`, so a failed save silently drops the match_count/last_match_at update while still returning the block decision; the "updates statistics" shared example only covers the happy path and no test covers a save that fails (severity P3, confidence 50, advisory)

spec/models/blocked_email_spec.rb:23 — `subject.should be_false` (RSpec 2 falsy matcher) accepts the `nil` that `record && record.action_type == actions[:block]` (blocked_email.rb:18) returns for a missing record, so the example does not pin the documented `false` return and a caller comparing `== false` would diverge unnoticed (severity P3, confidence 50, advisory)

The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.
